funder_origin_name: Wolf Foundation (endowment donated by Ricardo Subirana y Lobo Wolf and Francisca Subirana-Wolf)
funding_share_basis: 100% of the purse comes from investment income on the Wolf Foundation's own endowment, established in 1975-76 with roughly USD 10 million donated by Ricardo Wolf and his wife Francisca; the official site states the Foundation was 'Founded in 1975 with an endowment from the Wolf family' and no co-sponsor, corporate partner, or government appropriation for the purse is identified in any source. The Israeli state's involvement is governance and audit only (the Wolf Foundation Law-1975 makes the Minister of Education chairman of the Council and the State Comptroller the auditor), which is administration rather than purse money, so the >50% rule points to Philanthropy in both states.
money_note: Each Wolf Prize, including Physics, carries a diploma, a Medal of Honor, and USD 100,000, paid from the Wolf Foundation's endowment income; the prize has been awarded annually since 1978 and the 2025 Physics prize went to Jainendra K. Jain, Mordehai Heiblum, and James P. Eisenstein.
evidence_quote: Founded in 1975 with an endowment from the Wolf family, the Foundation's major donors were Dr. Ricardo Subirana Y Lobo Wolf and his wife, Francisca.
judgment_reason: A coder could call the Wolf Foundation Government (or Mixed) because it was constituted by the Israeli 'Wolf Foundation Law-1975', the Minister of Education and Culture serves ex officio as chairman of its Council, and the State Comptroller audits it. I coded Philanthropy for both the awarding body and the funder because the money is a private family endowment and the statutory role is governance/oversight, not payment of the purse.
